SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK CQL-21: CQL — Clinical Operators. Test these items: AgeInYears|Months|Weeks|Days|Hours|Minutes|Seconds(), AgeInYearsAt|MonthsAt|...At(asOf), CalculateAgeInYears|Months|...InYears(birthDate), CalculateAgeInYearsAt|MonthsAt|...At(birthDate, asOf), Equal (Code/Concept), Equivalent (Code/Concept), In (Codesystem), ExpandValueSet(ValueSet), In (Valueset). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 (2019May) Appendix B Clinical Operators: Age, AgeAt, CalculateAge, CalculateAgeAt — each operator 'is defined in terms of a date/time duration calculation ... if the birthDate is not specified to the level of precision corresponding to the operator being invoked, the result will be an uncertainty over the range of possible values'; AgeInYears/Months use Today(), other precisions use Now(); Age/AgeAt are shorthand for the equivalent CalculateAgeIn...At with the Patient-context birthDate.
issues.evidence: Probes .temp/qa/cql21_probe*.py. All age surfaces (translator bare AgeIn*() -> YearsBetween/MonthsBetween/... crisp UDFs; one-arg AgeIn*At(asOf) -> CalculateAgeIn*At; direct CalculateAgeIn*At UDFs) parse partial birthDates with a crisp day-1 convention and return a single integer on BOTH engines: CalculateAgeInYearsAt('2012','2026-05-14') -> 14 (spec: uncertainty [13,14]; duration surface cqlDurationBetween correctly returns {"start":13,"end":14}); CalculateAgeInDaysAt('2012','2012-02-28') -> 58 (spec range [-307..58]); end-to-end Patient context with FHIR birthDate '1990', AgeInYearsAt(@2026-05-14) -> 36 crisp (could be 35 if born after May 14) on py+cpp. Uncertainty-collapsing cases (e.g. '2012-06' vs 2026-05-14 -> 13) are already handled correctly by cqlDurationBetween, proving the semantics exist and age simply bypasses them. Comparisons (AgeInYearsAt(x) >= 18) therefore produce definitive booleans instead of possibly-null uncertain comparisons (cqlUncertainCompare machinery exists and is wired only for duration expressions). Equal/Equivalent Code+Concept, In(CodeSystem), In(ValueSet), ExpandValueSet re-verified conformant (CQL-02 doctrines intact, 15/15 parity tests pass).
issues.root_cause: Age surfaces bypassed the §22.21 duration-uncertainty engine: translator lowered bare AgeIn*() to crisp YearsBetween/MonthsBetween UDFs and one-arg AgeIn*At(asOf) to crisp CalculateAgeIn*At UDFs whose Python and C++ implementations parsed partial birthDates with a day-1 convention; _UNCERTAIN_BETWEEN_UDFS/_CQL_AGE_FUNC_NAMES uncertainty-comparison wiring did not cover the age family; and `x in Interval[a,b]` lowered to raw SQL BETWEEN over the now-VARCHAR age result.
issues.resolution: Fixture adjudication: the 1706-test CQL gate contains only 16 XML files (no CqlAgeOperatorsTest.xml), so no official fixture pins crisp partial-birthDate ages; spec prose governs. Routed all age surfaces through the §22.21 duration engine: Python udf/age.py rewritten to delegate to _duration_between_with_uncertainty (VARCHAR scalar-or-interval, negative-crisp→null, intervals surfaced); native age.cpp/cql_extension.cpp AgeFromStringTexts = AgeTextGuarded(CqlDurationBetweenString(...)); translator bare AgeIn*() → cqlDurationBetween(Today()/Now()), one-arg AgeIn*At(asOf) → CalculateAgeIn*At; age family added to _UNCERTAIN_BETWEEN_UDFS so comparisons go through cqlUncertainCompare; `in Interval[a,b]` over uncertain operands lowers to cqlUncertainCompare conjunctions (fixes 11 DQM BinderExceptions). Full-precision birthDates keep identical crisp results. Regression: test_cql_clinical_age_partial_birthdate_uncertainty_matches_cpp_registration (py+cpp) + updated test_age_udfs/test_clinical_operator_parity pins.

issues.evidence: Discovered at the unit-suite Recovery Gate, out of CQL-21 scope: test_logical_parity.py::test_cql_boolean_define_alias_feeds_logic_by_value fails — `define F: Patient.active; define G: F and true` raises TranslationError 'CQL logical operator and requires Boolean operands; got List<Any>'. At committed HEAD (db1e4164) the same library translates fine (F meta cql_type 'Any'); in the shared campaign tree F lowers to fhirpath_text and is marked _definition_is_dynamic_list -> cql_type List<Any> (CQL-19-era list semantics) which collides with _validate_boolean_operand (CQL-04-era guard). NOT caused by the CQL-21 age fix (age/interval-in changes are not on this path; bisect-verified vs HEAD). The master conformance gate (2832/2832) does not exercise this shape.
issues.root_cause: Single-valued FHIR property (Patient.active, 0..1 boolean) is classified dynamic-list by the fhirpath_text shape test without consulting element cardinality; the alias then fails boolean-operand validation.
issues.resolution: Deferred to the owning chunk (list/property typing, CQL-19 family). Suggested fix: gate _definition_is_dynamic_list on FHIR max-cardinality > 1 (schema metadata already resolves Patient.active as Boolean) or teach _validate_boolean_operand to look through stored-list aliases of Boolean-typed properties.
